en.html:
Standing in for the Lord of Horigoe at Fudaraku was, in fact, not proving particularly difficult. Not as difficult as I had prepared myself for, let us say. No need to congratulate me beyond the evidence.

Several reasons for this. The largest was probably the support team Chachamaru had provided.

A lieutenant colonel appearing overnight, origins unknown, and these men served him calmly and, for the moment, faithfully enough. Strange arrangement. Outwardly 'yes, sir,' inwardly 'who is this fellow?'—that would have been quite understandable.

Perhaps it was the nature of the Horigoe administration. To serve somebody like Chachamaru, one might have to cultivate the habit of obeying even an abnormal order without thinking. Thinking would only get in the way of completing the abnormality.

Or perhaps she had simply warned them before leaving. Either way, I did not expect their loyal service to continue indefinitely. About that, however, I was not troubled.

Acting lord, deputy, lieutenant colonel: all temporary arrangements. Why should I work hard at constructing beautiful relationships within the army? We needed to get along for the necessary period. No lifetime subscription was being requested.

On the many matters arriving daily, I asked for their opinions. They gave them. Experienced military bureaucrats, these men; their judgment was almost never wrong.

Half my work was talking to them. The remaining half, signature and seal.

Monotonous, with not one particle of originality. Still, I knew a general could function like this. In peacetime, a general determined to exhibit his individuality could be a much greater nuisance. During an emergency, perhaps different; otherwise, please keep your magnificent personality off the administration.

As a conscript, I had spent some time as a headquarters orderly. The general I served was of the no-individuality variety. I watched him closely. Listening to other people's ideas, he did far more of that than producing his own.

And yet he was called a master of military administration. Nobody governed occupied territory better. Then he was transferred, and a brilliant general arrived in his place. Before long, the locals rebelled.

Being brilliant, the new general would not listen to his staff. Everything according to his own ideas only. Which method was better for a general? Results-wise, at least, there was no room left for doubt.

So now I imitated that general, Higuchi. A certain irony in it, and a little repayment: six years ago, he had resisted Rokuhara's rebellion and been executed for his resistance.

普陀楽における堀越公方の代行は、実際、さほどの
困難もなく務まっていた。
　覚悟していたほどではない、という意味だが。

　それには幾つかの理由がある。
　特に大きいのは、茶々丸が用意した<ruby>補佐集団<rt>サポートチーム</rt></ruby>の存在
だろう。

　出自不明の俄か中佐に、彼らは淡々と、しかし一応
忠実に仕えてくれる。
　……奇妙といえば、これほど奇妙な話もない。面従
腹背の姿勢になって当然のところだ。

　あるいは、これは堀越公方府の性格なのか。
　茶々丸のような人間のもとで幕僚を務めるためには、
上司の時として異常な指示に対しても<ruby>考えず<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>服従する、
そんな習性を身に付ける必要があったのかもしれない。

　それとも単に、茶々丸が出がけに釘を刺していった
のか。
　どちらにしても彼らの俺への<ruby>忠勤<rt>・・</rt></ruby>が長続きするとは
思えないが、その点に関して俺は気に病まなかった。

　堀越公方の代行は勿論、副官も中佐も一時の方便に
過ぎないのである。
　軍内における良好な人間関係の構築を目指して努力
するなど、無駄であった。

　彼らとは必要な間だけうまくやれればそれで良い。

　日々持ち込まれる幾多の案件について、俺は彼らに
意見を求め、彼らは求めに応じて発言する。
　熟練した軍官僚である彼らの判断に、間違いはまず
無かった。

　俺の仕事は半分がた、彼らとの対話である。
　残りは署名と捺印だ。

　単調で独創性の欠片もない執務姿勢だが、将帥とは
それでも務まる事を俺は知っていた。
　むしろ個性を発揮したがる将帥の方が、非常事態の
折ならともかく、平時には煙たがられる事も。

　徴兵されて軍にいた頃の一時期、司令部付当番兵を
務めた。そのとき仕えた相手が無個性型の将軍だった。
　彼の振舞いを間近でつぶさに見たが、自分で知恵を
出すより他人の知恵を聞く方がずっと多かったと思う。

　しかしそれで、彼は軍政の名人と呼ばれていた。彼
ほど占領地を上手に治めた者はいなかった。
　彼はやがて転任し、代わって秀才型の将軍が来たが、
その新体制は程なく地元民の反乱を招いた。

　秀才ゆえ幕僚の意見を聞こうとせず、自分の考えで
全て断行した結果だった。
　将軍としてどちらの姿勢が正しかったか、少なくと
も結果論の範囲では疑問の余地がない。

　だから俺は今、あの樋口という名の将軍を模倣する。
　ある意味で、これは皮肉であり意趣返しだ――樋口
将軍は六年前、六波羅の反逆劇に対して抵抗したすえ
処刑されているのだから。

Assistant"Shall we process this matter as it stands, sir?"
Kageaki"I leave that to you."
Assistant"Yes, sir."
Kageaki"Where is the breakdown of the supplies?"
Assistant"Here, sir."
Kageaki"...The timber is short of the quantity ordered."
Assistant"Yes. Some was diverted to repairs on the castle gate. That much is missing."
Assistant"Shall I have the shortage made up urgently?"
Kageaki"Make it up, yes... but no need to squeeze everybody over it. As far as I can see, the original estimate is already quite generous."
Assistant"...That is true."
Kageaki"Even allowing for the venue's size, what we have should be enough. Leave it for now. When another order is needed, add the missing amount to that."
Assistant"Yes, sir. We shall do it that way."

en.html:
Inside the castle, preparations for the appointment ceremony were going ahead. Perhaps the Lord of Sasagawa's intimidation had worked: matters in Kyoto had taken a favorable turn, and Kuniuji Ashikaga's appointment as Lord General was approaching the final countdown.

Building the venue had fallen to the Horigoe administration. A small stroke of luck, this. In my days as a company employee, I had done such work until I was thoroughly sick of it.

All that accumulated know-how was finding plenty of employment now. Thanks to this luck also, I could wear the face of an acting lord without it sliding off entirely.

Today, especially, the construction matters kept coming. Examine one, take advice, deal with it. Then the next.
en.text:
Inside the castle, preparations for the appointment ceremony were going ahead. Perhaps the Lord of Sasagawa's intimidation had worked: matters in Kyoto had taken a favorable turn, and Kuniuji Ashikaga's appointment as Lord General was approaching the final countdown.

Building the venue had fallen to the Horigoe administration. A small stroke of luck, this. In my days as a company employee, I had done such work until I was thoroughly sick of it.

All that accumulated know-how was finding plenty of employment now. Thanks to this luck also, I could wear the face of an acting lord without it sliding off entirely.

Today, especially, the construction matters kept coming. Examine one, take advice, deal with it. Then the next.

ja.html:
城内では現在、宣下式典の準備が進められている。
　篠川公方の威圧策の効果あってか、京都情勢が好転
し、足利邦氏への大将領宣下が秒読み段階に入ったの
を受けての事だ。

　式典会場の設営は、堀越公方府の担当となった。
　これは小さな幸運と呼べたろう。会社員時代、俺は
この手の仕事なら飽きるほどこなしてきている。

　蓄えた<ruby>技術知識<rt>ノウハウ</rt></ruby>を活用する場には事欠かなかった。
　俺がそれなりに公方代行らしい面をしていられるの
には、この幸運もある。

　今日は特に、設営関係の案件が多かった。
　一つ一つ吟味し、助言を受けながら処理してゆく。

Workers and guards stood around, looking bewildered, while I heard the report. On the surface, a very straightforward matter.

Some materials were missing from storage. And no, they had not gone where they were meant to go and been used.

That had already been checked. No sign of use, yet gone.

Whatever procedure had removed them, it was not the correct procedure.

en.html:
For a thief, peculiar choices. Not goods that sold for much, as the officer said.

If money was the object, better things were available. Break into the castle of the rulers of Yamato and come away with this? Arre, after taking so much risk, at least let the profit stand up straight.

Still, I could not decide the whole case from that. Perhaps the culprit had weighed the risk of stealing, the risk of selling, and the return, then settled for something manageable. Small profit, small trouble. A modest thief. No grand dreams, no ambition to make his mother proud of the theft.

Such a calculation was possible also.
